title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 479-481, the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' section after La Longue Marche): Grothendieck builds an explicit group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Z of GL(2)-type. G = GL2; ρ and σ are two involutions of G; T_ρ is a torus; N'_σ is a normalizer-type subgroup. The aim is to receive the profinite Teichmüller-type group Γ_{0,3}^{+∧} ≅ SL(2,Ẑ)' and, more importantly, the objects 'M_{0,3}^~' that carry the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type action. Elements of M_{ρ,σ} are tuples (U, a, b), and elements of the 'S' (framed) version SM_{ρ,σ} are tuples (u, a, b, U). Here u lies in the Borel-type group B'_ρ, a in T_ρ, b in N'_σ, and U in G. They satisfy the determinant constraints (16): μ = det u = det U = det b = ε' det a, together with σ(b) = ε b.

This page converts that 'torsor-style' description into a 'transition-element' description. Previous-page (17) embeds SΣ (a set of tuples (α, β, f, μ, ε)) into G×G×G×G_m×μ_2. It is cut out by (det α)^2 = det β = det f = 1 and the 'loop-type' equation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε · β σ(β)^{-1} · ε_1(μ−1), where ε_1(ν) is the lower unipotent matrix with entry ν. Here G grants that the projection (19) to (α, β, f) ∈ G^3 is already a monomorphism: μ and ε are recoverable.

The group L_0 = Ker(det : B'_0 → G_m), elements ℓ·(1 λ; 0 1), acts by simultaneous left multiplication (20). One defines Σ^* = L_0 \ SΣ^× in (21). The map (22), (u, a, b, U) ↦ (α, β, f) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, u U^{-1}), is claimed to be an isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ SΣ. It is L_0-equivariant, with L_0 acting on u by left translation. Passing to the quotient gives (23), M_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ^*_{ρ,σ}.

This is the familiar elimination of base-point data: the 'path' u relative to local frames a, b, U is replaced by the three differences α, β, f. These are the analogues of the elements x, y, f appearing in the équation des lacets / GT relations. Finally, (24)-(25) give canonical homomorphisms S_0 M_{0,3}^~ → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ and M_{0,3}^~ → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ, with Σ = (μ_2)^3(Z) central. On Γ_{0,3}^{+∧} they agree with SL(2,Ẑ)' ↪ SG(Ẑ)/(SG ∩ Σ) (continued on the next page). So the page is a step in building a 'GL2 linear model' through which the Galois / GT-type action on the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller data factors.
errors: Notation slip: (21) defines Σ^* = L_0\SΣ^×, but (22) states the isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ SΣ^*. Since (23) is obtained 'par passage au quotient' by L_0, (22) should target the unquotiented SΣ^× (the previous page itself calls it SΣ^*). The ×/* superscripts are used inconsistently.
Consistency check of determinants: with det u = μ, det a = ε'μ (up to sign convention), det b = det U = μ, one gets det α = ε'^{±1}, so (det α)^2 = 1, and det β = det f = 1. This matches (17).
The main equation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε β σ(β)^{-1} ε_1(μ−1) cannot be verified from this page, since ρ, σ and B'_ρ are defined earlier.

Unproven claims: injectivity of (19) and the actual isomorphism (22) are asserted without proof. Bijectivity requires that u ∈ B'_ρ be recoverable from (α, β, f), which depends on the earlier definitions.
The final sentence is left incomplete on this page; it is continued on the next page as (26).

ideas.what: Re-parametrising a group of 'framed paths' (u; a, b, U) by the transition elements α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1}, then quotienting by the residual stabiliser L_0 (left translations of the frame u)
ideas.modern_name: Passage from fundamental groupoid with several tangential base points to a group via choice of base point / change of frame (gauge fixing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; in the GT context Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tangential base points and the Teichmüller tower qualitatively; this specific construction is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: An explicit Z-group scheme M_{ρ,σ} of GL2-type, defined by an 'équation des lacets'-type relation, receiving canonical homomorphisms from the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller data M_{0,3}^~ and extending SL(2,Ẑ)' ≅ Γ_{0,3}^{+∧} into M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ
ideas.modern_name: Linear (GL2/SL2) models of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / representations of GT-type groups into algebraic groups over Ẑ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related directions: Ihara (Galois action on pro-ℓ braids), Drinfeld (GT), Hain–Matsumoto (relative completion of mapping class groups), Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 'Longue Marche' continuation (cote 140-3)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit GL2-type group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Z, cut out by a 'lacets' equation with involutions ρ, σ and a unipotent twist ε_1(μ−1). He shows the genus-0 Teichmüller object M_{0,3}^~ (with its Galois-type action) maps canonically to M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ, compatibly with SL(2,Ẑ)'. Studying the induced representation of Gal(Q̄/Q), or of GT, into this explicit group does not appear to have been pursued as such.
missed.quote: On a des hom. canoniques (24) S_0 M_{0,3}^~ → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ (25) M_{0,3}^~ → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a concrete low-dimensional linear shadow of GT acting through 2×2 matrices over Ẑ. This could be compared with the abelianised and metabelian images of GT (Ihara power series, Anderson–Ihara) and with relative-completion approaches (Hain–Matsumoto). Its significance depends on the earlier definitions, which are not visible on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine change of coordinates (gauge fixing by L_0) inside a larger unpublished construction. The surrounding project, an explicit GL2-type Z-group scheme receiving the 3-point Teichmüller / GT data, is of some historical interest but is not fully visible here.
transcription_corrections: Middle paragraph: 'transformant l'action de Lo sur S[M]^*_{ρ,σ}' has the crossed-out symbol M overwritten. It refers to the action on SM_{ρ,σ}, with the inserted words 'par transport de l'action de Lo décrite dans (20), et induisant un iso'.
Last line: 'coïncidant sur Ĝ^{+λ}_{0,3}' should read 'coïncidant sur Γ^{+∧}_{0,3}', as confirmed by (26) on the next page.
(21): the struck-out text is a first attempt at the symbol Σ^*_{ρ,σ}; the definition reads Σ^*_{ρ,σ} =déf L_0\SΣ^×_{ρ,σ}.
The '543' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination; '480' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
'On fait opérer le groupe Lo' — 'le groupe Lo' is an interlinear insertion above the line.
